  title: Remote directories are still silently skipped
  claim: The new fallback only copies remote files, so the stated directory copy/paste case still completes without copying anything.
  detail: A TE directory represented by a location-less `DBNResource` has no `Path`, and it cannot provide the newly requested `InputStream` because that adapter is limited to `IFile`; `dropNodes` then continues and refreshes the target, falsely appearing successful. Directory copy must either be implemented recursively or fail explicitly rather than silently dropping the selected directory.
  evidence: DBNPathBase.java:289-301 enters the new fallback and continues when the stream adapter is null; DBNResource.java:420-425 returns null for a location-less `IFolder` and only adapts `IFile` to `InputStream`; NavigatorHandlerObjectCreateCopy.java:100-104 invokes this path for clipboard paste.
  fix: Handle directory resources according to the copy contract, or reject them with a visible error before reporting completion.
- path: plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.model/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/model/navigator/fs/DBNPathBase.java
  line: 293
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P2
  confidence: 0.98
  reachability: routine
  kind: resource-management
  title: Acquired remote file streams are never closed
  claim: The stream-based copy path leaks the `IFile.getContents()` stream for every pasted remote file.
  detail: `DBNResource.getAdapter(InputStream.class)` opens an `IFile` content stream, then `dropNodes` passes it to `Files.copy` without a try-with-resources; unlike the existing stream consumers, no owner closes it after successful or failed copying. The copy path must close every stream it obtains.
  evidence: DBNResource.java:423-425 obtains the stream from `file.getContents()`; DBNPathBase.java:293-297 passes it to `copyInputStream`, whose Files.copy call at line 369 does not close its input; NavigatorHandlerObjectCreateCopy.java:211-213 and NavigatorDragSourceListener.java:180-184 demonstrate existing callers close comparable streams.
  fix: Wrap the locally acquired adapter stream in try-with-resources around the copy.

  title: The new remote-stream paste behavior has no regression coverage
  claim: This behavior change ships without a test covering the location-less resource and stream-adapter branch it introduces.
  detail: The fix depends on `Path` being absent, `InputStream` being supplied by `DBNResource`, and the stream being copied into the target folder, but the PR changes only the two production files. A regression test must exercise that seam so future adapter or drop-path changes cannot silently restore the original no-op.
  evidence: The PR diff contains only DBNResource.java and DBNPathBase.java; the guarded branch is DBNPathBase.java:289-301, with its source adapter added at DBNResource.java:423-425.
  fix: Add a regression test that pastes a location-less `IFile` resource into a DBNPath target and asserts copied content and failure behavior.

  kind: correctness
  title: Stream-backed paste leaks the source stream
  claim: The new stream-backed paste path never closes the `InputStream`, leaking remote file handles/connections on every successful paste.
  detail: `getAdapter(InputStream.class)` opens an `IFile` stream and `Files.copy(InputStream, Path, ...)` consumes but does not close it; repeated TE file pastes can therefore exhaust the backing EFS resources. The copy path must own and close every stream it opens.
  evidence: DBNPathBase.java:293 obtains the stream and :296 passes it to `copyInputStream`; :359-365 only calls `Files.copy`. DBNResource.java:423-425 opens it with `IFile.getContents()`. The existing paste implementation closes the same resource with try-with-resources at NavigatorHandlerObjectCreateCopy.java:233-235.
  fix: Use the existing `DBNStreamData.supportsStreamData/openInputStream` seam and wrap the returned stream in try-with-resources while copying.

  fix: Wrap the acquired InputStream in try-with-resources before copying it.
